title: Texas surface faults (Geologic Database of Texas, 1:250,000)
source: USGS, TxGIO (TNRIS), BEG and TWDB (2007). Geologic Database of Texas, Fault250K layer, from the BEG Geologic Atlas of Texas sheets
note: Faults mapped at the ground surface at 1:250,000 (locations good to about 100 to 250 m). A surface trace says where a fault reaches the surface, not where it is at injection depth.

title: Gulf Coast regional faults and fault zones (USGS, after Ewing and Lopez 1991)
source: USGS (2004). Faults in the Gulf Coast [gcfaultsg] and Fault Zones in the Gulf Coast [gcfltzoneg], digitised from Ewing, T.E. and Lopez, R.F. (1991), Principal structural features, Gulf of Mexico basin, GSA DNAG Plate 2
note: Regional, schematic trends of growth faults and fault zones at depth (Balcones, Luling, Mexia, Talco, Frio, Vicksburg, Yegua, Miocene). A trend line, not a located fault plane at a given depth.

title: Permian Basin basement-rooted faults (BEG, Horne et al.)
source: Horne, E.A. et al. (2021, 2022) Basement-rooted faults of the Delaware Basin and Central Basin Platform, v4, doi:10.18738/T8/UHOUX8; Horne et al. (2023) Midland Basin faults and Greater Permian Basin regional v1.0, doi:10.18738/T8/ZTBOGP. Bureau of Economic Geology / TexNet, Texas Data Repository
note: Faults interpreted from 3-D and 2-D seismic and well data at basement and Ellenburger level, with confidence and dip where given. The most relevant public map for deep Permian injection; still an interpretation at regional scale.

title: Quaternary (young) faults (USGS Quaternary Fault and Fold Database)
source: U.S. Geological Survey and Texas Bureau of Economic Geology, Quaternary fault and fold database of the United States
note: Faults with evidence of movement in the last 1.6 million years. In Texas these are in the Trans-Pecos only.

title: TexNet earthquakes, magnitude 2 and above, 2017 on
source: TexNet Seismic Monitoring Program, Bureau of Economic Geology, earthquake catalog
note: A snapshot taken when this build was made. Earthquakes can mark active faults that no map shows.
